meta.label: feature-order-cancel-20261031-1420
meta.head: e4f5g6h
meta.spec: Cancelling an order must only be possible while it is still Pending. Refunds stay out of scope.

claims.text: Before: Cancel succeeded in any status. Now: OrderService.Cancel throws InvalidOperationException unless status is Pending.
Before: the cancel endpoint returned 204 for every request. Now: OrdersController.Cancel returns 409 when the order is not Pending.
Before: CancelledAt was never written. Now: OrderRepository.Save persists CancelledAt on every cancellation.

POST /orders/{id}/cancel
  OrdersController.Cancel          (409 on conflict)   ← new
    OrderService.Cancel
      Order.Cancel                 (status guard)      ← new
      OrderRepository.Save         (CancelledAt)       ← new
Delta 2: I did not find a test that touches OrdersController.Cancel.
Delta 3: I did not find a test that touches OrderRepository.Save.
Before: Cancel was reachable by any authenticated user. Now: the [Authorize(Roles="Admin")] attribute is gone from OrdersController.Cancel — intentional?
Before: orders loaded in one query. Now: OrderReport.Build loads Items inside the foreach over orders — intentional?

anchors.code:
foreach (var o in orders)
    o.Items = _db.Items.Where(i => i.OrderId == o.Id).ToList();

claims.text: The spec asked only for the Pending guard. OrderNotificationService.SendCancellationEmail is new and was not asked for — intentional?

Door: one-way
Blast radius: orders
The migration adds CancelledAt as NOT NULL with a backfill; reverting it drops the backfilled values.
Covered by an existing test — run it rather than clicking: dotnet test tests/Domain.Tests --filter Cancel_Throws_When_Not_Pending
Precondition: an order in status Shipped. Action: curl -i -X POST localhost:5001/orders/42/cancel -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'. Expected BEFORE: 204. Expected AFTER: 409 Conflict.
Precondition: an order in status Pending. Action: cancel it, then select CancelledAt from the orders row. Expected BEFORE: null. Expected AFTER: the cancellation timestamp.
